species.name: Crappie
why: Water 65°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 8–30 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is mixed top to bottom, so fish can use many depths.

species.name: White bass
why: Water 65°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 10–34 ft deep, mostly on open water over the deep basin.
The lake is mixed top to bottom, so fish can use many depths.
Northwest wind at 15 mph pushes bait onto the southeast shore: try the wind-blown banks.

species.name: Largemouth bass
why: Water 65°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 2–20 ft deep, mostly on wind-blown banks.
The lake is mixed top to bottom, so fish can use many depths.
Northwest wind at 15 mph pushes bait onto the southeast shore: try the wind-blown banks.

species.name: Catfish
why: Water 65°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
Best water today is 8–38 ft deep, mostly on wind-blown banks.
The lake is mixed top to bottom, so fish can use many depths.
